title: Best Milk for Toddlers: 10 Types & Nutritional Guide
text:
Beyond the simple glass of milk, the world of dairy offers a diverse range of tasty and nutritious options. From creamy cheeses to protein-packed puddings, this article explores various dairy products and their unique nutritional profiles.Discover the benefits and understand the nutritional value of these delicious dairy delights!
Beyond the Glass: Exploring Diverse Dairy Delights and Their Nutritional Profiles Milk is frequently enough touted as a cornerstone of a balanced diet, notably for children, due to its rich calcium content. However, the world of dairy extends far beyond a simple glass of milk. from creamy cheeses to protein-packed puddings,a variety of milk-based products offer unique nutritional benefits and culinary experiences.
Dairy’s Role in a Balanced Diet For infants, breast milk is the gold standard, followed by complementary foods (MPASI) up to two years of age. Pediatrician Dr. Aisya Fikritama, Sp.A, notes that children over one year old can incorporate other types of milk into their diets. However, she emphasizes that solid foods should remain the primary source of nutrition.
Giving milk to children over the age of 1 year both breast milk and other milk is not the main because it can only be given a maximum of 30 percent of the total calorie needs, and the remaining 70 percent should be in the form of solid food.
Dr. Aisya Fikritama, Sp.A
Dr. Fikritama further clarifies the role of milk in a toddler’s diet:
So milking in the context of foods of toddlers and toddlers is a source of calcium and a source of protein with complete essential amino acids.
Dr.aisya Fikritama, Sp.A
A Deep Dive into Dairy Products and Their Nutritional Values let’s explore a range of dairy products, each offering a distinct nutritional profile:
1.Soft Cheese Soft cheese is known for its smooth texture and mild flavor. Here’s a glimpse into its nutritional content per serving:
Carbohydrates: 0.60 g Fiber: 0 g Sugar: 0.08 g Fat: 9.46 g Saturated Fat: 5.43 g Protein: 6.78 g Cholesterol: 27.7 g sodium: 180 g 2. Butter Butter, a high-fat dairy staple, is created by churning milk or cream. It’s a versatile ingredient used as a spread and for cooking. Butter is a source of vitamins A and D. One tablespoon (14.2 grams) contains:
Calories: 102 kcal Carbohydrates: 0.01 g Fiber: 0 g Sugar: 0.01 g Fat: 11.5 g Saturated fat: 7.17 g Protein: 0.12 g Cholesterol: 30.5 mg Sodium: 1.56 g 3. Whey Whey, a byproduct of cheese production, is a protein powerhouse. Whey protein boasts a protein density of 70-90%, depending on the product. A 100-gram serving of standard whey protein offers:
Calories: 352 kcal Carbohydrates: 6.25 g Fiber: 3.1 g Sugar: 0 g fat: 1.56 g saturated Fat: 0.78 g Protein: 78.1 g Cholesterol: 16.0 g Sodium: 156 g 4. Casein Casein, comprising about 80% of the total protein in cow’s milk, is derived from skim milk. It’s a significant source of calcium, providing approximately 50% of the daily requirement. Calcium supports vital functions like bone, muscle, and blood vessel health.A 30-gram serving of unflavored casein powder contains:
Calories: 110 Fat: 0 g Sodium: 25 mg Carbohydrates: 0 g Fiber: 0 g Added Sugar: 0 g Protein: 24 g Calcium: 579 mg 5. Cream Cream, a high-fat milk product, consists of a layer of butterfat that rises to the top of milk before homogenization. With fat contents ranging from 18% to 55%, cream provides vitamins A and D. while rich in saturated fat and not exceptionally nutrient-dense,it offers a distinctive flavor. 15 grams of thick cream contain:
Calories: 51 kcal Carbohydrates: 0.43 g Fiber: 0 g Sugar: 0.43 g Fat: 5.42 g Saturated Fat: 3.45 g Protein: 0.43 g cholesterol: 17 g Sodium: 4 g 6. sweet Condensed milk Sweet condensed milk is a dairy product with most of its water content removed and sugar added for sweetness. ir. Doddy Izwardi,MA,Director of Community Nutrition,advises against giving sweet condensed milk to children under five due to its high sugar content.
This sweet thickness is not intended for toddlers… The sugar content is very high, so it is indeed not intended for it.
Ir. Doddy Izwardi, MA
A 38.2-gram serving of sweetened condensed milk provides:
Calories: 123 kcal Carbohydrates: 20.8 g Fiber: 0 g Sugar: 20.8 g Fat: 3.32 g Saturated Fat: 2.1 g Protein: 3.02 g Cholesterol: 13 g Sodium: 48.5 g 7. Gelato Gelato,an Italian frozen dessert,is made with cream,milk,sugar,and optional ingredients like chocolate,fruit,and nuts. Gelato uses a higher proportion of milk and less cream than ice cream,resulting in a smoother,softer texture. One 160-gram spoonful of chocolate gelato contains:
Calories: 402 kcal Carbohydrates: 31.7 g Fiber: 1.44 g Sugar: 27.8 g Fat: 27.2 g Saturated Fat: 16.6 g Protein: 7.55 g Cholesterol: 96 g Sodium: 91.2 mg 8. Quark Quark,a soft fermented cheese originating from Germany,is known for its high protein content. It has a mild, creamy, and slightly sour taste. Produced using cream milk and fermented lactic acid, quark is low in fat and carbohydrates.150 grams of quark provide:
Calories: 91 kcal Carbohydrates: 5.5 g Fiber: 0 g Sugar: 5.5 g Fat: 0.5 g saturated Fat: 0 g Protein: 17.5 g Sodium: 50 g 9. Protein Pudding Protein pudding, a high-protein milk product, is typically made from cream milk, milk protein, thickener, flavoring, and sweetener. It offers a protein-rich snack option with lower calories, available in flavors like chocolate and vanilla. 128 grams of protein pudding contain:
Calories: 106 kcal Carbohydrates: 1.6 g Fiber: 0.8 g Sugar: 0 g Fat: 2.4 g Saturated Fat: 0.3 g Protein: 20.0 g cholesterol: 4 g Sodium: 43 g
